John McCarthy wrote:
> 
> emclean@slip.net (Emmett McLean) writes:
> 
> > TK wrote the following which applies to the concept of hates crimes :
> >
> >
> > > Consequently the leftist is never satisfied with the goals he has already attained;
> > > his need for the power process leads him always to pursue some new goal. The
> > > leftist wants equal opportunities for minorities. When that is attained he
> > > insists on statistical equality of achievement by minorities. And as long
> > > as anyone harbors in some corner of his mind a negative attitude toward some
> > > minority, the leftist has to re-educated him. And ethnic minorities are not
> > > enough; no one can be allowed to have a negative attitude toward homosexuals,
> > > disabled people, fat people, old people, ugly people, and on and
> on and on.
> 
> But not on indefinitely.  One is certainly allowed to have a negative
> attitude to rednecked people.

	Actually no.  There have been attempts to install the idea of "hate
crimes" as a means of suppressing hateful speach and beliefs by
non-minorities, but my impression is that this has failed.  "Hate crime"
is not a crime in itself, but a motive that makes the crime more
heinous, and therefore "enhances" the potential penalties.  It seems to
be judged on the basis of whether the person was harmed or the damage
was done because the target was a member of a social category, no matter
what that category may be.  Minorities have no special protection. 
Anyone could be the target of a hate crime.

Scott
